`python -m pytest tests -q` now runs against the working tree — and this is the discharge.

**Why the earlier runs needed `PYTHONPATH=src`:** `.venv` was created with `--system-site-packages` and had no `attrs` of its own, so `import attr` resolved to a stale copy in user site-packages (pytest's hypothesis plugin imports it at startup, before the root `conftest.py` can prepend `src/`). The bare command was testing the wrong code — which is why it reported 7 failures. I installed the project editable into `.venv` (`uv pip install -e .`); `attr.__file__` now points at `src/attr/__init__.py`. No repo files changed for this.

**Result:** `2 failed, 1386 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed`.

The 2 failures are `test_packaging.py::TestLegacyMetadataHack::test_version_info[attr|attrs]`:

```
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'dev1'
  VersionInfo._from_version_string('0.1.dev1')
```

This seeded repo has no version tag, so hatch-vcs stamps `0.1.dev1` and `VersionInfo` can't parse the `dev1` segment. Pre-existing and unrelated — I verified by stashing all my changes (`git stash -u`) and re-running: **the same 2 tests fail on the pristine tree** (1385 passed / 2 failed). My changes add 3 passing tests and remove none.
